extracted.intended_audience: poets, creative writers, and readers/students of literary theory interested in imagination, memory, and the creative process
extracted.subtask_description: Philosophical guidance on the mental faculties (imagination, memory, will, attention) relevant to poetic and prose composition, including practical conditions that aid recollection and the productive creative process. Emphasises voluntary control of imagination, attention, and the alternation of active/passive mental states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perspicuity (clarity of expression)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive 'to be as perspicuous as the nature of language will permit' when treating subtle subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author explicitly solicits readers' patience while attempting clarity on abstruse matters; implies a standard that writers should aim for maximum possible clarity given linguistic limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination as intermediate faculty (active and passive control)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagination is the intermediate faculty that is at once both active and passive; in poetry the term denotes a superior degree of this faculty joined to superior voluntary control over it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composition requires this intermediate power; superior poetry manifests both a high degree of imaginative power and voluntary control (the ability to direct and shape imaginative operations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary attention / will as determinant of vividness
rubrics_metrics.description: The will, by confining and intensifying attention, may arbitrarily give vividness or distinctness to any object whatsoever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should use deliberate, willed attention to intensify elements they wish to make prominent; this is preferable to passive or mechanical methods of memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts/conditions of Memory
rubrics_metrics.description: The best (and only) arts of Memory are: sound logic; philosophical knowledge of facts under cause-and-effect; a cheerful and communicative temper; a quiet conscience; freedom from anxieties; sound health; and above all, a healthy digestion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memory and reliable recollection for composition depend on overall mental, moral, and bodily conditions; cultivating these is part of a writer's craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternation of active and passive mental states in composing
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of composing involves alternate pulses of active and passive motion—resisting and yielding—in the mind, analogous to a little insect advancing against a current.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should recognise and work with this rhythm: periods of deliberate effort and resistance followed by yielding/receptive intervals are part of productive composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of association: continuity, contemporaneity, likeness, contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: Association depends on contemporaneity (co-presence in time), continuity/contiguity, likeness, and contrast; these are the causes by which ideas recall each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing, understand which associative principle (time, space, similarity, contrast) produces a recall or linkage; this can be used deliberately to shape imagery and transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salience within impressions determines recall
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever makes certain parts of a total impression more vivid or distinct than the rest will determine the mind to recall those in preference to others equally linked by contemporaneity or continuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To control what a reader (or the writer's mind) remembers, enhance the vividness/distinctness of chosen elements within an impression (through emphasis, detail, repetition, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject mechanical/artificial schemes that debase the fancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Recent schemes promising an artificial memory are useless or absurd and in reality produce confusion and debasement of the fancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying on mechanistic shortcuts or purely artificial mnemonic systems at the cost of imaginative quality; prefer cultivation of attention, health, and moral temperament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sound logic and causal understanding in composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Sound logic (habitually subordinating the individual to the species, species to genus) and philosophical knowledge of facts under cause and effect aid memory and the illustration of similarities and contrasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A disciplined logical understanding and appreciation of causality strengthen the writer's ability to order material and to use analogy and contrast effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict immediate perception (immediacy of the object) rather than inferred impact
rubrics_metrics.description: In immediate perception the object itself, not merely its inferred effect or the product of a syllogism, is present to consciousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should aim to render objects as immediately present to the reader's mind, avoiding over-intellectualised mediations that turn perception into inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish conditions of perception from causes (avoid category mistakes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not mistake the conditions of a thing (e.g., contemporaneity as condition for association) for its causes and essence; confuse the process of arriving at knowledge with the faculty itself at your peril.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise in critical thought and description: elucidate processes (how an impression arises) without misattributing them as the essence of the idea or faculty being described; this clarity aids credible imaginative writing and theorising about mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral discipline precedes intellectual persuasion
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who adopt erroneous systems often need moral improvement, not argument; 'Such men need discipline, not argument; they must be made better men before they can become wiser.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When aiming to change minds (through writing), consider moral and temperamental cultivation as part of the writer's ethical project; rhetorical argument alone may not suffice for certain readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve a sense of agency against mechanistic reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: A theory that reduces will, reason, and understanding to mechanical products makes the soul 'a mere motion' and is unacceptable for explaining human creativity and moral responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In creative representation and theory, avoid reducing human agency to purely mechanistic explanations; sustain the sense of active authorship and moral intentionality in characters and in the writing process itself.
